subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Barking up the wrong tree

options.text: To make a bad situation worse
Getting a good start is important
To be mistaken, to be looking for solutions in the wrong place

solution:
The correct answer is: **'****To be mistaken, to be looking for solutions in the wrong place****'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Barking up the wrong tree"** means to be mistaken, or to be looking for solutions in the wrong place. (गलत जगह पर समाधान ढूंढना)
 
• **​"Mistaken"** refers to being wrong about something, often due to a misunderstanding or incorrect information. (गलतफहमी)
 
 
• **Example: **She was mistaken about the meeting time, thinking it was an hour later than it actually was.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Provoke trouble** (मुसीबत पैदा करना): To cause problems or conflict.

 
 
• **Example:** His rude comments were only meant to **provoke trouble** among the team members.
 
 
 
• **To make a bad situation worse** (खराब स्थिति को और बिगाड़ना): To take actions that exacerbate an already negative situation.
 
 
• **Example: **By lying to cover up his mistake, he only **made a bad situation worse**.
 
 
 
• **Getting a good start is important** (अच्छी शुरुआत महत्वपूर्ण है): Emphasizes the importance of starting something well.
 
 
• **Example:** In any race, **getting a good start is important** to increase your chances of winning.
